newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot gas prices remain firm amid western heat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot gas prices remain firm amid western heat.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices remained firm Tuesday ahead of the release of storage data later today, as the return of heat to the Southwest fueled a price uptick in California, industry sources said.
"All in all, prices were pretty flat. Depending on AGAs, I don't see these prices moving very much," one Houston-based trader said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast gas at the Henry Hub traded in a wider range of $2.17-2.23 per mmBtu, as NYMEX's 1.2 cent decline to a low of $2.135 put some pressure on cash mid-morning, traders said.
In south Texas prices slipped about one cent to $2.08-2.10. Temperature highs in Houston through Thursday were expected to drop a few degrees to the low-90s F.
News surfaced this afternoon that severe storms left about 152,000 power customers in Houston without service today, Houston Lighting and Power reported, noting additional power outages were likely.
In the East, New York city gate prices were in the mid-$2.40s, indicating a gain of about one to two cents from Monday.
Temperatures in the Northeast were expected to average near normal through Thursday before turning warmer Friday and into this weekend, Weather Services Corp (WSC) reported.
In the Midwest, prices gained about two cents to $2.04-2.06 due most likely to storage injection demand, traders said.
Chicago city-gate was quoted equally firmer at $2.21-2.23.
Mostly normal temperatures are forecast to continue in the Midcontinent throughout most of this week, according to WSC, with temperature highs in Chicago forecast in the mid-70s F.
In west Texas, Permian prices gained another three cents to the low-$2 area as temperatures in southern California warmed to highs in the mid-80s F.
Southern California prices were sharply higher at $2.19-2.25.
Adding to the tightened supply was the outage at El Paso Natural Gas Co's Blanco natural gas plant in the San Juan basin.
The plant, which has the capability of processing about one billion cubic feet per day of gas, is scheduled to remain shut through Saturday for annual maintenance.
As a result, the pipeline will cut capacity by by 815 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) on Tuesday and Wednesday. Flows will be cut by 415 mmcfd on Thursday and by 240 mmcfd on Friday and Saturday.
Capacity on the North Mainline for deliveries to Topock and South markets will be cut by 195 mmcfd through Thursday for pipeline replacement.
Separately, injection estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report have ranged from 78 to 110 bcf, versus a gain of 87 bcf a year ago.
